workouts.name: 4km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Your recent runs have held cadence around 150-160 spm, well below the 172-174/min turnover this plan targets in the Peak-phase speed sessions. Use today's strides to actively practice quicker, lighter steps now, while there's no fitness cost to experimenting.

briefing.purpose: Easy volume plus neuromuscular priming — strides teach fast, relaxed turnover without fatigue, and set up the next quality day.
briefing.structure: 3.3 km easy @ 4:35-5:03/km → 6× (Stride — fast & relaxed @ 3:30-3:45/km / 45s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km)
briefing.feel: Easy throughout; strides are fast and springy, ~90% effort, never sprinted.
briefing.if_wrong: Strides feeling forced or heavy-legged? Cut them — the easy running is the session; strides are a bonus.

workouts.name: 4km Tempo Run

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: This lands with the near-daily indoor cardio/HYROX-style classes still running in the background most mornings — that combined load is part of why training readiness dipped into the 20s through late July. If today's legs feel heavier than the pace suggests, respect RPE 7 over the split.

briefing.purpose: Lactate threshold — raises the pace you can sustain. The single biggest lever for Base-phase fitness at your distance.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 4 km tempo at threshold pace @ 4:04-4:18/km → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Comfortably hard, RPE 7. You could speak a sentence, not hold a chat.
briefing.if_wrong: Too hard? Slow 5-10 s/km rather than stopping — the aerobic stimulus survives a slower tempo, not a broken one. Heat or hills: switch to effort.
briefing.cue: Lock the rhythm with your breathing (e.g. 2:2) and let pace follow it.

workouts.description: Maximal-effort benchmark. Race it like race day — warm up properly, pace evenly, empty the tank. The result recalibrates your training paces.

steps.description: 15 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Your last hard benchmark predates this cycle — the paces above come from Garmin's VO2 Max (53.4), not a fresh time trial. Today's result recalibrates every pace band in this plan for the next five weeks, so run it honestly rather than pacing to a number an algorithm produced.

briefing.purpose: Benchmark — an honest maximal effort measures fitness better than any formula, recalibrates your training paces, and doubles as race practice.

briefing.if_wrong: Conditions bad (heat, wind, illness)? Postpone rather than run a false benchmark — a wrong number miscalibrates every pace that follows.
briefing.venue: Flat, repeatable course (or parkrun/track) — same venue each time.
briefing.warmup: Treat the warm-up like race day: 15min easy + drills + 3 strides, then 2min standing rest before the start.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Cadence target here is explicitly 174 — recent runs have mostly logged 150-160, so the biggest win today is turnover, not raw speed. Let the pace follow quick feet rather than forcing it.

briefing.purpose: Speed and running economy — short, fast reps recruit fast-twitch fibres and sharpen form, making every slower pace cheaper.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 10× (200m fast & relaxed — mile race effort @ 3:30-3:45/km / 60s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Fast, springy and light — ~95%, never an all-out sprint. Full recovery is part of the design; R work only counts when you're fresh for each rep.
briefing.if_wrong: Form breaking (shoulders up, overstriding)? Stop the set — junk reps train junk form. These reps are about quality, never volume.
briefing.warmup: After the easy warm-up: 2-3 drills (high knees, A-skips) plus 2-3 strides — fast reps on a cold engine is how calves tear.
briefing.cue: Think 'fast feet on hot coals' — ground contact short, heels never settling.
briefing.venue: Track or a measured flat stretch — GPS pace lies over 200-400m, so run these by effort and check splits after.

workouts.name: 5 x 3.0min VO2max Intervals

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Same 172 cadence target as the Peak-phase speed session, this time under more fatigue since it's VO2max intensity.

briefing.purpose: Aerobic ceiling — short hard reps at ~3K-5K effort push maximal oxygen uptake, which everything below it hangs from.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 5× (3.0 min hard — 3K-5K race effort @ 3:42-4:00/km / 3.0 min recovery jog @ 4:35-5:03/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Hard, RPE 8-9. Controlled discomfort — the last rep matches the first.
briefing.if_wrong: Fading before the final rep: slow 5 s/km or take 30s more recovery. In heat or wind run by RPE 8 — the pace window assumes calm, flat ground.
briefing.warmup: After the easy warm-up: 2-3 drills (high knees, A-skips) plus 2-3 strides — fast reps on a cold engine is how calves tear.
briefing.cue: Relax the face and hands on the back half of each rep — tension is free speed lost.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Broken threshold with short recoveries — a gentler mental load than a straight tempo, useful this close to race day when accumulated fatigue from months of HYROX-plus-running is real.

briefing.purpose: Lactate threshold in pieces — same stimulus as tempo with the mental load broken up. Floats/recoveries keep the lactate shuttling.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 4× (6min at threshold @ 4:04-4:18/km / 60s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km

briefing.if_wrong: Fading mid-set: slow 5 s/km, don't bail. If floats become jogs, you started too fast — that's the lesson, bank it.

workouts.description: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
workouts.notes: Race day. Whatever cadence and pacing habits got reinforced in the strides and speed sessions are what shows up now — trust them.

briefing.purpose: The day it was all for. Nothing new today — the kit, fueling and pacing you rehearsed are the plan.
briefing.structure: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
briefing.feel: First third controlled (it should feel too easy), middle third rhythmic, final third everything you have left.
briefing.if_wrong: Bad patch mid-race? They pass — ease 5 s/km for 2 minutes, take fuel, rebuild. Never surge to 'make up' time.
briefing.fuel: Race-day intake exactly as rehearsed on the long runs.

weeks.intro: Race week. The work is banked — nothing you do now makes you fitter, plenty can make you tired. Short, sharp, rested.

rationale: Built around your actual recent running volume (13.5 km/week, VDOT 53.4 from Garmin) rather than a generic half-marathon template — you're layering this on top of frequent HYROX-style conditioning (near-daily indoor cardio sessions, Anaerobic-Focus training load), so weekly running mileage stays deliberately lean while it builds. The two weeks before this plan started showed Strained training status with Unbalanced/Low HRV; readiness only returned to Balanced/Recovery on the day the plan began, so Base phase opens conservatively before Build ramps up.
tips: Cadence has sat at 150-160 spm on recent runs; the Peak-phase speed and VO2max sessions target 172-174 — use the strides days now to close that gap early, not in Peak phase when fatigue is higher.
RPE logging is sparse (one real entry so far) — log it after key sessions so the coach has more than pace and HR to react to.

Keep tracking morning readiness and HRV; a repeat of late-July's Strained stretch is the trigger to trade a quality day for an easy one that week, not a reason to abandon the plan (paceforge adapt applies this automatically).
The near-daily indoor cardio classes are real training load even though they're not running mileage — factor them in when the plan looks light on paper.
